ellie: Hey team — new POC request from BeaconCorp. They want a drop-in replacement for CompetitorX endpoints. Primary asks: request/response parity, streaming behaviour, cost delta, and enterprise security questionnaire. Can we list what to validate first?
omar: At minimum: header mappings, auth differences, streaming format, stop-token handling, and tokenization differences (e.g., competitor uses a different tokenizer).
lucas: I'll own the mapping work. Noted CompetitorX expects `CX-Client` header and uses SSE `data:` frames. We use Authorization + chunked JSON. Suggest writing a tiny HTTP adapter. Example (Python flask proxy):
```
from flask import Flask, request, Response
import requests
app = Flask(__name__)
@app.route('/v1/compat/generate', methods=['POST'])
def compat():
    headers = {'Authorization': request.headers.get('Authorization'), 'x-request-id': request.headers.get('CX-Req-Id')}
    resp = requests.post('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate', json=request.get_json(), headers=headers, stream=True)
    return Response(resp.iter_content(chunk_size=2048), status=resp.status_code, content_type='application/json')
```
kevin: For billing: client reports ~1.8M tokens/month on CompetitorX. We need to show token accounting differences: our tokenizer may split differently which affects billed token count. Recommend we run 1000 sample prompts from their logs through both tokenizers.
ellie: Also they care about latency — CompetitorX gives <90ms p95 for simple generation. We should capture p50/p95 on our Hosted and note Dedicated recommendations.
omar: Security asks: SSO (SAML), customer KMS, VPC peering, data retention policies, and audit log access. For Hosted, we support SAML SCIM for enterprise, but VPC peering is Dedicated/Private only. Call out that.
security-bot: New security intake created: SEC-IN-9876 assigned to @kevin and @omar. Please attach questionnaire answers within 72 hours.
kevin: I'll draft KMS answers — we offer CMKs on Dedicated and Private; for Hosted we provide envelope encryption and SOC2/CIS attestations. Will include rotation policy and key ownership text.
lucas: On output parity: aside from tokenization, stop-sequence behaviour differs. CompetitorX honors a list of stop tokens sent as array; our API accepts `stop` but semantics vary on partial matches. We'll create paired test cases showing differences.
ellie: UX streaming: they rely on SSE event:delta chunks with progress markers. Our SDK exposes incremental delta chunks with JSON fields `choices[].delta`. I'll include a sample client shim for browser SSE -> our chunk mapping.
omar: Ops note: CORS and preflight may be different; if they were using CDN edge hooks with CompetitorX, we need to verify any origin restrictions.
kevin: License models: they asked if committed monthly spend can be converted into a reserved throughput block. Yes — Dedicated offers committed GPU pools; we'll produce a template commit aligned to their current spend + 10% headroom.
ellie: Action items:
